NUEVO LAREDO, Tamaulipas — The Nuevo Laredo customs house took first place nationally in tax collection for September 2026, bringing in 16.379 billion pesos — equal to 14.7 percent of all of Mexico's customs revenue for the month, according to data released by the Tamaulipas state Secretariat of Economy and reported by Central de Noticias Tamaulipas.

The numbers underline just how dominant the Neolaredo border corridor has become. In a single month, the port processed 498,523 foreign trade operations, more than a quarter of the entire national volume (26.5 percent), and handled 22 percent of all customs declarations filed across the country.

A trillion-peso anchor

Consolidated records from Mexico's National Customs Agency (ANAM) confirm that the local aduana contributes more than a trillion pesos a year to federal coffers, while consistently concentrating over 40 percent of bilateral overland trade between Mexico and the United States.

The state Economy Secretariat said the density of cargo flow and the port's strategic position back continued public investment in regional logistics infrastructure — chief among them the development of ANAM's national headquarters in this border municipality.

Sources: Central de Noticias Tamaulipas (Oct. 22, 2026); data from the Tamaulipas Secretariat of Economy and Mexico's National Customs Agency (ANAM).

title: Nuevo Laredo customs takes national #1 spot with 16.379 billion pesos collected in September
